title: Find Maximum Area of a Triangle
summary: Given a 2D array of coordinates, determine twice the largest area of a triangle with at least one side parallel to the x-axis or y-axis, or return -1 if no such triangle exists.
statement: Given a 2D array of coordinates, determine twice the largest area of a triangle with at least one side parallel to the x-axis or y-axis, or return -1 if no such triangle exists.
constraints: coords has up to 100,000 distinct points with positive coordinates.
Choose a nonzero-area triangle having a horizontal or vertical side.
Return twice its maximum area, or -1 when none exists.
hints: For a vertical base at x, the longest base uses extreme y values and the greatest height uses the farther global x extreme.
Group y extrema by x, combine with global x extrema, then swap coordinate roles for horizontal bases.
For every x compute (maxY-minY)*max(x-minX,maxX-x); repeat with x and y exchanged.
Base and perpendicular height independently increase area, so replacing either by its available extreme cannot worsen a qualifying triangle.
editorial: Base and perpendicular height independently increase area, so replacing either by its available extreme cannot worsen a qualifying triangle.

tests.explanation: A vertical base of length one and horizontal height two gives doubled area two.
No pair shares an x or y coordinate, so no qualifying triangle exists.
